about: Local inputs for the ten-year property cost and maximum-price model. Every value is tagged reported, modeled or assumed and names a source_id in data/sources.csv. 'reported' means a published figure, but often for a wider area than the site (state average, metro proxy); read 'scope' before using it. No CoStar, Vexcel or Matterport data is in this file.

conventions.electricity_usd_per_kwh: all-in retail energy price per kWh of facility (not IT) load
conventions.wue_l_per_kwh: litres of on-site water consumed per kWh of IT energy
conventions.water_usd_per_kgal: volume charge per 1,000 US gallons, excluding meter/base charges

houston.label: Houston, TX (City of Houston, Harris County)

electric_utility.note: Houston is in the competitive ERCOT market; CenterPoint is the delivery utility. A large-load bill must be built from the retail contract plus CenterPoint demand and rider charges.

electricity_usd_per_kwh.note: State average is not a CenterPoint large-load tariff and excludes demand-charge structure.

build_cost_usd_per_w.scope: Dallas benchmark used as a Texas proxy; Turner & Townsend publishes no Houston figure
build_cost_usd_per_w.note: Benchmark is ~60 MW air-cooled build-to-suit; excludes land, utility works, IT equipment, fees (S03). Applying it to a small retrofit is an assumption.

land_usd_per_acre.scope: Harris County Appraisal District 2026 land values for vacant commercial lots on the same block as the Jensen Dr demo property
land_usd_per_acre.note: Appraised land value, not a sale price. Lee & Associates reports Houston industrial land up 40-50% over two years (V09), so market prices may run above appraisal.

detention_usd_per_acre.scope: Houston industrial development, panel remark, Sep 2026
detention_usd_per_acre.note: Stormwater detention can add roughly this much per developed acre. Applies to new site work, not to reuse of an existing building footprint.

water_usd_per_kgal.scope: City of Houston commercial water volume charge, effective 2026-04-01
water_usd_per_kgal.note: Excludes meter-size base charge, TCEQ fee and drainage. Wastewater applies to cooling-tower blowdown, not to evaporated water; confirm the sewer billing basis.

water_stress.note: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 baseline water stress at the demo property (stored per site in Tiger `sites.water_stress_label`).

utility_connect_usd.note: New service for ~1.8 MW facility load (1.5 MW IT at PUE 1.2) on a greenfield site: line extension, transformer, metering, protection. No sourced CenterPoint figure; replace with a utility estimate. Sensitivity 0.5M-2M.

benchmark_site.about: A hypothetical typical powered greenfield site in the Houston market sized for 1.5 MW IT. Used as the comparison site for the price ceiling. It is not a real listing.

mw.note: Same IT load as the demo properties.

acres.note: Room for a ~10-15K SF building, generators, parking and detention. No sourced footprint for this size.

askingPriceTotal.note: Powered land at $584K per MW x 1.5 MW (Cushman & Wakefield 2026, primary US markets average). Cross-check: HCAD appraises unpowered vacant commercial land near the demo property at ~$200K per acre (V08).

detentionUsd.note: Stormwater detention for 1 developed acre at ~$750K per acre (Houston panel remark). Greenfield only; add to site cost, not land.

buildCostUsdPerW.note: Same Texas proxy as the market build cost.

waterUsdPerM3.note: $9.34 per 1,000 gal / 3.78541 m3. Water volume charge only.

checks.detail: Assumed: a powered site by definition (the land price includes the power premium). Source: assumption.
Houston-area Aqueduct baseline water stress is Medium-High, matching the demo property. Source: S05.
Houston has no citywide zoning; assumes a site with no restrictive deed covenants. Source: V17.
Assumed: site chosen away from homes and schools. Source: assumption.
Assumed: same Texas policy context as the demo property, which scores Low on the model. Source: M01.
Assumed: outside the 1% and 0.2% FEMA flood zones. Source: assumption.
Houston metro construction employment 269.3K in Sep 2026, up 5.4% year on year. Source: V15.

los_angeles.label: Los Angeles, CA (City of Los Angeles, LA County)

electric_utility.note: The demo parcel is inside the City of Los Angeles per the County Assessor, which implies LADWP service. Not confirmed against a utility service-territory map; neighbouring Vernon has its own utility.

electricity_usd_per_kwh.note: The state average is dominated by PG&E and SCE. LADWP commercial/industrial rates are likely lower; no official LADWP 2026 C&I average was found. Using the state figure biases the LA site toward higher cost. Replace with an LADWP A-2/A-3 bill build when available.

build_cost_usd_per_w.scope: Silicon Valley 2026-27 figure used as the California proxy; no Los Angeles figure is published in the index
build_cost_usd_per_w.note: Silicon Valley value comes from a secondary report of the T&T index, not the T&T page itself. Same scope exclusions as S03.

land_usd_per_acre.scope: LA County Assessor 2026 roll land value for the Perrino Pl demo parcel ($11,316,827 / 3.172 ac)
land_usd_per_acre.range_note: Low: 2022 base-year land value $10,455,000 / 3.172 ac (V07). High: one Q2 2026 off-market LAX-area land sale at $135 per land SF, reported in Kidder Mathews' Q2 2026 LA industrial report (V10, read from a search summary only).
land_usd_per_acre.note: Prop 13 assessed value tracks the 2022 transfer, not 2026 market. A private CoStar sale-comp summary (median improved industrial ~$7.1M per lot acre, n=8) is in data/private/inputs/ and must not be committed.

water_usd_per_kgal.scope: LADWP Schedule C (commercial/industrial) Tier 2 total consumption charge inside the City, Jul-Dec 2026: $14.513 per HCF / 0.748
water_usd_per_kgal.tier1_note: Tier 1 $10.529 per HCF / 0.748. A data center's cooling use would sit mostly in Tier 2.
water_usd_per_kgal.note: Excludes service charges and sewer fees.

water_stress.note: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 baseline water stress at the demo property.

utility_connect_usd.note: New LADWP service for ~1.8 MW facility load on a greenfield site. No sourced LADWP figure; replace with a utility estimate. Sensitivity 0.5M-2M.

benchmark_site.about: A hypothetical typical powered greenfield site in the Los Angeles market sized for 1.5 MW IT. It is not a real listing. It fails the water check like every LA site under the current rule, so it cannot be the eligible alternative.

mw.note: Same IT load as the demo properties.

acres.note: Same footprint assumption as the Houston benchmark.

askingPriceTotal.note: 1 acre at the LA County Assessor land value of the demo parcel ($3.57M per acre). The V04 powered-land average ($876K for 1.5 MW) is a primary-market average and would understate LA.

buildCostUsdPerW.note: Silicon Valley used as the California proxy.

electricityUsdPerKwh.note: California industrial average, Aug 2026; LADWP is likely lower.

waterUsdPerM3.note: LADWP Schedule C Tier 2, $19.40 per 1,000 gal / 3.78541 m3.

checks.detail: Assumed: a powered site by definition. Source: assumption.
Los Angeles basin Aqueduct baseline water stress is Extremely High (>80%). Source: S05.
Assumed: an industrially zoned (M2/M3) parcel. Source: assumption.
Assumed: site inside an industrial district. Source: assumption.
The Texas-trained model does not score California; no California policy review done. Source: M01.
Assumed: outside FEMA flood zones. Source: assumption.
LA-Long Beach-Anaheim construction employment 251.5K in Sep 2026, flat year on year. Source: V16.

wue_l_per_kwh.note: Evaporative cooling tower, Table 3 of Akinade et al. 2026; value is the range midpoint.

pue_multiplier.note: Baseline. Apply to the team PUE assumption (1.2, S19) in web/lib/model.ts.

V02 lists 1.25-1.40 relative PUE (25-35% power penalty). Uptime Institute (V03, Apr 2026) finds well-designed dry systems can match evaporative PUE across ASHRAE zones 2-6, so the low end of the range is 1.0. Default uses V02's low end.

capex_delta_usd_per_w.note: No sourced capital-cost difference between dry and evaporative heat rejection was found. Treated as equal; the cooling toggle changes operating cost only. Flag this in the UI.

us_all_in_greenfield_usd_per_mw.note: Cushman & Wakefield 2026 guide, all-in excluding chips/GPUs, via secondary summaries. Power infrastructure ~21% and site acquisition ~7% of total.

powered_land_usd_per_mw.note: Primary US markets, 2026 YTD, via secondary summary.

maintenance_rate.note: Annual maintenance as a fraction of build cost. No sourced figure; team assumption. Use the range for sensitivity.

gaps: LADWP large commercial/industrial tariff (A-2 or A-3) bill build; the LA electricity value is a state average.
CenterPoint large-load delivery charges for Houston; the Houston electricity value is a state average.
Utility connection cost: filled with assumed values, not sourced. Replace with utility estimates.
Annual maintenance rate: filled with an assumed 0.02, not sourced.
Benchmark site footprint (1 acre for 1.5 MW): assumed.
Houston land sale comps (public); only appraisal-district values are used.
